title: Power Apps: calendar and card layouts for views in model-driven apps
notes: 2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the briefing labels the layouts admin-opt-in and included at no cost, although the roadmap allows maker configuration and does not establish licensing or cost. The general grid settings have documented automation, and the briefing overstates what is known about the new layouts' controls and behaviour.

claims.fix: Set defaultState to user-opt-in: the standard includes maker-chosen designer capabilities in that value, and targeted searches found no documented separate admin gate for this new feature.

claims.claim: The layouts are included in an existing licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps new view layouts calendar stack cards model-driven app designer admin enable setting license; model-driven calendar layouts license. Read create-edit-views and model-driven app licensing excerpts; none establishes inclusion.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown and retain 'Not yet published' in Cost and licensing; neither the roadmap nor the Microsoft documentation found establishes inclusion.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licensing terms for the new layouts have been published in the sources found.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps new view layouts calendar stack cards model-driven app designer admin enable setting license; model-driven calendar layouts license. Read create-edit-views and model-driven app licensing excerpts; no terms for these layouts were found.

claims.claim: The cost rating is none despite licensing being unpublished.
claims.quote: cost: "none"; Cost and licensing: "Not yet published."; rationale: "None published. No licence or consumption change is described for the new layouts."
claims.fix: Set cost to low for the app review, accessibility checking and communication effort identified by the page. Start the rationale 'Low.' and explicitly state that licensing is not yet published; the standard reserves none for documented inclusion.

claims.claim: The environment grid settings are under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Grids and views.
claims.quote: select Manage ... select Environments ... select an environment ... select Settings ... Expand Product, and then select Features. ... Grids and views

claims.claim: Automation for the general environment grid and view settings is not documented.
claims.quote: AdvancedColumnEditorEnabled ... Flag to indicate if the display column options on a view in model-driven apps is enabled ... LogicalName ... advancedcolumneditorenabled
claims.fix: Replace the broad API absence with documented automation for the relevant individual organization setting, or remove this general-control row. The writable advancedcolumneditorenabled setting and pac env update-settings are documented; cite this reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/env#pac-env-update-settings. Do not describe that setting as controlling the new layouts.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: A tenant or environment switch for the new calendar and card layouts is not yet documented on either surface.
claims.quote: Searched: model-driven calendar card admin layout; Power Apps new view layout. Read settings-features and create-edit-views; results document older controls, not a switch for the new layouts.

claims.claim: The new layouts can be enabled independently per view.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps new view layout; model-driven calendar card admin layout. Read create-edit-views and add-calendar-control excerpts. The roadmap specifies the app designer, not per-view granularity.
claims.fix: Replace 'per app or view', 'per view' and 'makers opt views into them' with 'configured by makers in the model-driven app designer, according to the roadmap'; add configuration granularity to Open questions.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn documentation specifically describing these new layouts was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps new view layout; Power Apps calendar and card; Power Apps calendar stack of cards. Opened create-edit-views; read add-calendar-control and create-card-forms excerpts. These describe existing views and controls, not the roadmap's new layouts.

claims.claim: The new layouts leave data unchanged.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps model driven views calendar card layout security table column permissions. Read create-edit-views and model-driven app security documentation. None states that these new layouts leave data unchanged or describes their editing behaviour.
claims.fix: Remove 'Data ... unchanged' as a guarantee. Say 'The roadmap describes a presentation choice; detailed data-editing behaviour is not yet documented.'

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The layouts introduce no new data access and only display existing view data.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps model driven views calendar card layout security table column permissions. Read create-edit-views and share-model-driven-app; neither states a feature-specific no-new-access guarantee.
claims.fix: Frame this as analysis: 'The roadmap describes alternative presentation of model-driven app data, so we expect limited data-boundary change; detailed behaviour is not yet documented.' Remove the unconditional 'No new data access'.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Model-driven app table security continues to govern access to records.
claims.quote: a security role contains privileges that define a set of actions that can be performed on tables within the app
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/share-model-driven-app for the general model-driven app table-security statement; do not imply that this documents all new-layout behaviour.

claims.claim: Existing column security applies to data accessed in the layouts.
claims.quote: Column-level security configurations are organization-wide and apply to all data access requests.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/field-level-security to sources for the general column-security statement.

claims.claim: The layouts introduce no autonomy or actions.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps new view layout; Power Apps model driven views calendar card layout security table column permissions. Read create-edit-views and older calendar-control excerpts; none specifies the new layouts' action capabilities.
claims.fix: Replace 'None' with 'The roadmap describes no autonomous capability; available record actions are not yet documented.'

claims.claim: The layouts arrive with the model-driven app runtime.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps new view layout; Power Apps new view layouts calendar stack cards model-driven app designer admin enable setting license. Read create-edit-views and settings-features; neither documents this new feature's runtime delivery mechanism.
claims.fix: Remove 'they arrive with the model-driven app runtime'; retain only the roadmap's documented maker configuration in the app designer.

claims.claim: There is no admin control for the new layouts themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: model-driven calendar card admin layout; Power Apps new view layouts calendar stack cards model-driven app designer admin enable setting license. Read settings-features and create-edit-views. No source states there is no admin control; absence of documentation is narrower.
claims.fix: Replace 'There is no admin control for the new layouts themselves' with 'No separate tenant or environment switch for the new layouts was found in Microsoft documentation as of November 2026.'
